value.body: A two-year master's degree in commerce. It goes deeper into accounting, finance, taxation, business economics and research methods, often with an elective area such as Finance, Accounting & Taxation, Banking or Business Analytics. It is the usual route to teaching commerce and to a PhD, and it is often combined with professional courses or competitive exams.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 4 semesters; also widely offered in distance and open mode

items.label: Students enrolled
items.note: All modes; about 7.8% of all postgraduate enrolment

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Com (some universities also accept BBA, BBM or B.A. Economics, sometimes with a minimum percentage). Central universities admit through CUET-PG; many state universities use their own entrance test or bachelor's-degree marks, and some states run a common PG test.

value.title: At a glance
items: A master's with 55% (50% for reserved categories) makes you eligible for UGC-NET, the test for lectureship and PhD admission.
Many students pursue M.Com alongside CA, CMA or CS, or while preparing for banking and government exams.
Regular-mode enrolment has stayed roughly flat at around 3–3.5 lakh over five years.
